starting_observation_and_chain: (1) DATO: d-APV 50 uM eliminated the spontaneous bursts and the effect reversed (34634460 Results 2.2; 51 bursts, 5 slices, 3 animals; legend). -> (2) DATO: no AMPA/kainate antagonist was applied and the text has one AMPA word; AMPA dependence is untested within the perimeter of the paper text and supplement. -> (3) INFERENZA: the knockout mEPSC amplitude distribution is shifted to larger events at -70 mV with a decay of about 5 ms (5.18 vs 4.84 ms), the kinetic signature of an AMPA-type quantum; the pooled-event KS p values are inflated and are not used as confirmation, and the sEPSC mean differs by only about 6 percent. -> (4) IPOTESI: AMPAR current is a required step in burst initiation, with NMDAR current required for the burst as d-APV shows (burst-onset reversal about 6 mV is compatible with any glutamate cation channel). -> (5) IPOTESI, benefit: if bursts need AMPAR current, an AMPA-directed question (class transfer from the felbamate/perampanel nomination) becomes testable in this slice; if bursts survive a verified AMPA block, that question is dropped for this preparation

decision_measure: A verified-complete AMPA block that spares bursts removes the AMPA arm; a block that abolishes bursts at less total charge removed than d-APV needs puts AMPAR first in the next pharmacological question. Neither can be replaced by literature on other epilepsy models, and NBQX or GYKI use needs a mechanism paper that was not reached. NEW MEASUREMENTS (not literature): within-slice paired design (each slice its own baseline, replacing the pooled-baseline unpaired comparisons of the source); recording Mg2+ and K+ as measured bath values; a receptor-agnostic release-reducing control; a floor control for the delayed-response metric.

starting_observation_and_chain: (1) DATO: bursts need NMDAR activity at the d-APV concentration used (OB04); the delayed evoked response is larger in the knockout (about 0.46 vs about 0.12 mV at 100 uA, INFERENZA from the figure) and is reduced by d-APV to about 0.4 of baseline at 100 uA and overshoots on washout (about 1.3), but the amplitude metric has a floor (wild type reads about 0.115 mV), so against the floor about 20 percent of the delayed component remains (INFERENZA); the residual is not used as evidence of incomplete block (Fig S3; OB08, OB09). -> (2) DATO: no isolated NMDAR current, subunit, glycine or Mg2+ datum exists for this preparation; recording Mg2+ not stated; resting potential is 5.6 mV more depolarised (Table 1). -> (3) INFERENZA: NMDAR dependence of the burst can arise from NMDAR gain, from permissive necessity in a depolarised, less inhibited network, or from AMPAR-led drive; these are not separated (module card F04). -> (4) IPOTESI: a GluN2B-containing component sustains the burst beyond what total NMDAR current predicts (curve left of matched d-APV). -> (5) IPOTESI, benefit: a pharmacological question can then be posed at the receptor-composition level instead of 'any antagonist'; coincident curves instead say the question is about total gain

corrections_it40: Step 4 ('sufficient to explain') is a possibility from a culture result, not a slice result; the package's own audit leaves no datum for the gap-junction half. The experiment BE4 line calling perampanel, radiprodil and carbenoxolone non-reversible is not supported: perampanel has a recovery time constant of about 3.3 s in culture, and the radiprodil washout datum is from oocytes. Predictions in the arms are INFERENZA from the hypothesis definitions; no cell is a measured result.
status: IPOTESI; exploratory; premise not established; independent audit: PARTLY, close to a withdrawal of the gap-junction attribution. What survives: the direction-only reading of the carbenoxolone result, the off-target evidence from culture (with IPSC reversible and EPSC incomplete), the absence of any Panx1 engagement or connexin-selective test in the slice, and the measurement plan (EPSCs, spike width, coupling, matched controls); no datum in the sources read separates the gap-junction half from the off-target explanations (the carbenoxolone fall is not inconsistent with a coupling contribution; it is unattributable)
starting_observation_and_chain: (1) DATO: carbenoxolone 100 uM cut burst frequency strongly and the effect did not recover on washout (text 87 percent mean-normalised; Table S1 median 0.84 to 0.03 per minute; Fig 3D bar about 0.1); the magnitude, the n (36/4 vs 13/6) and the amplitude statement are disputed between text, table and figure, so only the direction and the non-recovery are used. -> (2) DATO: the source itself says carbenoxolone may block NMDA receptors and blocks pannexin channels; brilliant blue FCF 10 uM did not lower burst frequency (median 0.84 to 0.78; n 73/6 vs 25/6) without any Panx1 engagement check. -> (3) DATO: in autaptic mouse hippocampal culture carbenoxolone 100 uM reduced AMPA EPSC to 63 percent and NMDA EPSC to 69 percent with a higher paired-pulse ratio (presynaptic), broadened spikes, lowered input resistance and reduced IPSCs (rapidly and fully reversible), while the EPSC reduction recovered incompletely; the AMPA-only glutamate-current test (95.7 percent) was run with NMDAR blocked, so direct NMDAR channel block was neither shown nor excluded. In rat CA1 slices carbenoxolone 100 uM (alone at P12, together with La3+ at P20) did not significantly change the reversed-uptake ischaemic glutamate current (P12 mean 22 percent lower, n = 6 against 14, P = 0.46, so an effect of the size found in culture is not excluded). -> (4) INFERENZA: the burst fall cannot be assigned to gap junctions; an effect on release and excitability is sufficient to explain it. -> (5) IPOTESI, benefit: the gap-junction half of the module's NMDAR-or-gap-junction wording stays withdrawn until a matched-effect control and a cleaner discrimination exist
context: Neuron-specific Wwox knockout neocortical slices P13-P17 as in the source; culture data are mouse hippocampal micro-island neurons (P0-P1 origin, 6-15 DIV, room temperature), CA1 slices are rat P12/P20 at 33 C; transfer to the burst preparation is unmeasured
competing_explanations: Carbenoxolone acts through reduced release or excitability (H5); NMDAR block (H5, unresolved); Panx1 contributes (H6) but BB-FCF engagement is unverified; time-dependent run-down (M02); non-gap-junction K+ and Ca2+ effects of mefloquine
premise_and_action: Distinguish carbenoxolone's release, excitability and NMDAR effects from connexin or pannexin coupling by measuring EPSCs, spike width and coupling in the burst slices and by a matched-effect control
compound_or_probe_named_by_package: Carbenoxolone (19535488; 20940167; 23589583 Fig 6: blocks mouse Panx1 in oocytes, concentration not stated) as the compound whose off-target effects were read; brilliant blue FCF (23589583: Panx1 IC50 0.27 uM, plateau 75 to 85 percent in oocytes, no block of P2X7 or Cx46/Cx32E143 at 100 uM) with a Panx1 engagement measurement still to be made; mefloquine only if a primary mechanism and slice side-effect reading is obtained (abstract: Cx36 IC50 about 300 nM in N2A cells, 25 uM blocked interneuron coupling in neocortical slices, increased spontaneous synaptic activity); genetic ablation or dominant-negative approaches are the standard named by the Tovar authors

A catalogue target record says where the mechanism was attached (one protein, a two-gene assembly or a family), not how selective the molecule is
source_and_limits: The Tovar culture result points to a sizeable presynaptic release effect; Madry's CA1 result is low-powered against a 20-30 percent effect (22 percent lower, P = 0.46, n = 6 against 14) and reads a reversed-uptake ischaemic glutamate current, not evoked release, so it neither contradicts Tovar nor excludes an NMDAR block and carries little weight; both are kept, neither is slice data from this preparation || weakening: Carbenoxolone and a non-gap-junction manipulation matched to the same measured EPSC reduction produce the same burst fall (M10): H6 not supported and the coupling question not worth a connexin-selective arm; or brilliant blue FCF with demonstrated engagement lowers bursts (Panx1 supported)
decision_measure: A measured carbenoxolone effect on the slice's EPSCs large enough to account for the burst fall settles the attribution as non-gap-junction for this preparation; a residual burst fall beyond the matched control with coupling loss keeps the connexin question open. No literature on other preparations substitutes for the EPSC, spike and coupling measurements in these slices. NEW MEASUREMENTS (not literature): within-slice paired design; recording Mg2+ and K+ as measured values; a receptor-agnostic release-reducing control; two metrics for matched controls.

corrections_it40: Independent recomputation (IT40 verifier) gives standard-error multiples for the flat-tau argument of about 1.1 to 1.4, not the 3.9 and 2.9 quoted in the chain; read the chain's multiples as not reproduced. The argument also assumes a single compartment and a protocol that does not shorten the apparent tau. Predictions in the arms are INFERENZA from the hypothesis definitions; no cell is a measured result.
status: survives as an exploratory, qualitative hypothesis (flat tau against pure leak loss is supported; implied capacitance, step 5 as first written and the HT-KO gradient were weaker than written and are corrected here); no Wwox conductance datum exists; decisive probes are abstract level or unread
starting_observation_and_chain: (1) DATO: Rin 102.88 / 143.26 / 143.03 Mohm, tau 18.55 / 18.79 / 21.25 ms, rest -79.25 / -75.51 / -73.62 mV (34634460 Table 1; O01-O03). -> (2) INFERENZA: tau flat while Rin rises 39 percent argues against a PURE leak loss at constant capacitance (predicted tau about 25.8 ms against 18.8 and 21.3, about 3.9 and 2.9 SE below); this holds under the single-compartment assumption and a hyperpolarisation-activated conductance in the 50-60 ms fit window could also shorten the apparent tau, so it supports "something besides a pure leak loss", not specifically "smaller cells". -> (3) INFERENZA: implied capacitance tau/Rin about 180 / 131 / 149 pF reproduces but carries about 14 percent propagated uncertainty (WT versus HT z about 1.6, WT versus KO about 1.1) and does not follow the dose order: a lower capacitance in mutants is a direction of means, not an established difference. A smaller cell with unchanged specific resistance gives Rin up and tau flat; it does not by itself depolarise rest, but smaller cells plus a fixed seal leak (A10) would give Rin up, rest depolarised and tau flat, so the depolarised rest needs a second cause (fewer open K+ channels, seal or recording factors, or network state, MH3). -> (4) INFERENZA: with a fixed -200 pA step the larger Rin drives HT and KO cells about 8 mV further (about 20.6 versus 28.7 mV), to peaks of about -101, -106, -105 mV on the recorded scale, so absolute sag and rebound in mV can rise with no change in HCN. -> (5) INFERENZA: E_K is about -97 to -98 mV and needs no junction correction; the recorded potentials do (about -13 mV, borrowed): on the corrected scale the peaks are about -114 / -119 / -118 mV, 16-21 mV BELOW E_K, so K+ current at the sag peak is inward and not small; the prediction that a K-leak difference current reverses near E_K belongs to the voltage-clamp experiment E3 (zero crossing at the corrected E_K), not to the sag peak. -> (6) benefit: none claimed; a measurement hypothesis that decides whether any pharmacological arm is needed for the sag at all.
context: Mouse neuron-specific Synapsin-Cre Wwox deletion, layer II/III pyramidal neurons, P13-P17 acute slices at 35 C, littermate Cre+ controls; endpoint: sag, rebound and Rin at matched potential and matched deflection, capacitance, tau, Ba2+- or XE991-sensitive current; no exposure (ex vivo).
competing_explanations: MH2 (an HCN contribution that remains after matching); A05 recording factors (access resistance, selection by Rin and tau); A10 smaller cells plus a fixed seal leak; A04 maturation delay; A06 network state.
premise_and_action: None proposed. A leak or Kv7 opener would hyperpolarise and lower Rin in wild-type and mutant cells alike, so a response would not show a leak deficit (a drug response is not proof of a defect in its target).
compound_or_probe_named_by_package: None nominated. Kv7 openers (retigabine: abstract states KCNQ2, KCNQ3, KCNQ2/3 and KCNQ4, not KCNQ5, and native M channels in rat sympathetic neurons; SCR2682: abstract names rat hippocampal or cortical neurons) were read at abstract level only; XE991 was not read; K2P and Kir tool papers exist (reported by the verifier: ML133 for Kir2 and ML335/ML402 for TREK-1/TREK-2 in heterologous systems, not read by me) but none is shown to work in layer II/III pyramidal neurons. No compound is justified on this basis.

A catalogue target record says where the mechanism was attached (one protein, a two-gene assembly or a family), not how selective the molecule is
source_and_limits: F-I slope unchanged (O09) is a constraint not explained; sag fraction still rises in crude group means (5.4 to 8.2 percent) but with about 1.6 propagated SE between WT and KO, so it is not established; the HT-versus-KO difference in sag (t about 0.9) and rest (t about 0.8) is NOT used against MH1 (not distinguishable); flat tau may be a protocol artefact (tau and Rin from different protocols). || weakening: Matched potential and matched deflection (or a Rin-normalised sag ratio) removes the genotype difference in sag and rebound AND voltage-clamp capacitance is lower in mutants AND Ba2+- or XE991-sensitive current per pF is unchanged -> passive size explains most of Rin and sag; the reading fails if sag remains at matched conditions (MH2), if capacitance is unchanged while Rin is higher, or if the Ba2+-sensitive difference current does not reverse near the corrected E_K in the E3 voltage-clamp experiment. Smaller-cell versus seal-leak versus leak loss is separated by E1 plus E3 only if seal and access resistance are reported.

corrections_it40: The package describes the Ih blocker ivabradine as nonselective across HCN isoforms; the catalogue holds only an HCN4 mechanism row for it, which is a record granularity, not a selectivity. Predictions in the arms are INFERENZA from the hypothesis definitions; no cell is a measured result.
status: survives only as a conditional, exploratory hypothesis: its premise (a residual excess sag at matched conditions) is not established and is testable only with matched data (E1); rests on abstract-level or untested items for the decisive datum (no Ih in Wwox cells; ZD7288 off-target numbers abstract level; Kv7 and T-type probes abstract level); the Fig 5 reading confirms a partial sag reduction, not abolition
starting_observation_and_chain: (1) DATO: sag 1.18 / 2.04 / 2.57 mV and rebound 0.96 / 1.24 / 1.86 mV at a fixed -200 pA (O04, O10); the authors infer an elevated Ih from the larger deflection (O11); no voltage-clamp Ih exists. -> (2) INFERENZA, premise NOT established: a residual sag excess after matching would indicate a larger HCN contribution or shifted gating; the crude sag fraction 5.4 / 6.6 / 8.2 percent carries about 1.2-1.6 points of propagated uncertainty (WT versus KO z about 1.6, WT versus HT about 0.7), Ih activation is steeply voltage dependent so a fraction can rise with unchanged HCN density when the step reaches 4-5 mV deeper, and the HT-versus-KO difference at equal estimated deflection is not distinguishable (t about 0.9); the premise is UNVERIFIABLE without per-cell sag, Rin and deflection. -> (3) DATO (transfer): an HCN blocker REDUCES sag in normal cortical layer 5/6 neurons (ivabradine, 34018186, rat 25-35 d, Fig 5 viewed: about 2.65 to about 1.4 mV at -200 pA, n=6) and in thalamic neurons (ZD7288 20 umol/L, 24953239: residual 0.4-2.1 mV from 4-6 mV, with a 15-18 mV hyperpolarisation), so HCN contributes to sag in those cells; DATO at abstract level: ZD7288 also blocks T-type current (extracellular application, CA1) and sodium current (DRG, Nav1.4). -> (4) INFERENZA: a second chemotype plus a voltage-clamp subtraction can assign an excess sag to Ih; without both it cannot (the thalamic authors themselves note possible T-type window-current contamination of the ZD7288-subtracted current). -> (5) benefit: unknown in direction; an increased Ih is not assumed harmful. The GAERS authors expect Ih-driven burst suppression to be seizure-reducing, discuss a compensatory origin and then say any compensation is unlikely to be directly related to SWD development; they do not call the Ih rise harmful; in GAERS more Ih came with lower peak-based Rin, unchanged rest and unchanged sag (A09), not the Wwox pattern.
context: Mouse neuron-specific Wwox deletion, layer II/III pyramidal neurons, P13-P17, acute slices 35 C, bath exposure of the tool at a concentration verified for engagement; endpoints: ZD7288- and ivabradine-sensitive sag at matched conditions, Ih density per pF and V1/2 in voltage clamp, then burst incidence.
competing_explanations: MH1 (passive and leak reading); T-type contribution to rebound (Z944 arm, hcn_20261107 X4); sodium-current off-target of ZD7288; a different HCN isoform or compartment.
premise_and_action: HCN blockade as a TOOL arm in slices (two chemotypes, engagement first), reading sag, rebound, Rin, rest and burst incidence in the same slices; no candidate drug and no in-vivo claim.
compound_or_probe_named_by_package: Tool classes only: ZD7288 (sag reduction and hyperpolarisation read in 24953239 full text, Fig 6 viewed) and ivabradine (sag reduction and hyperpolarisation read in 34018186 full text, Fig 5 viewed; described by the authors as a nonselective inhibitor of HCN isoforms). Not nominated as treatments; ivabradine in vivo needed an efflux inhibitor to reach about 184 nmol/L free brain level (n=4), and the slice concentrations were micromolar.
catalogue_by_action: R4: 3 catalogue rows = 2 distinct parent molecules on the target symbols (a record is repeated per gene symbol); 2 reduce activity, 0 raise it or have no direction; single_protein_record: 2. A catalogue target record says where the mechanism was attached (one protein, a two-gene assembly or a family), not how selective the molecule is
source_and_limits: GAERS (24953239): more Ih with lower peak-based Rin, unchanged rest and sag; ZD7288 lowered Rin (authors: unexpected) at a 15-18 mV more negative potential. Neocortical ZD7288 study cited by 34634460 reported Rin up (secondhand; its abstract, 27464853, gives no such numbers). Review (37982354) says open HCN lowers Rin; Wwox Rin is up. A blocker-mediated sag reduction does not show an HCN defect. || weakening: At matched potential and deflection the sag and rebound excess disappear, or ZD7288- and ivabradine-sensitive current per pF and V1/2 are the same in KO and WT -> no HCN difference; MH2 retained only as a statement that HCN contributes to sag as it does in normal cortex. Sag reduced by a blocker with burst incidence unchanged supports HCN in sag, not benefit; burst incidence rising is not by itself compensation either.
decision_measure: A matched-condition excess sag in KO that is blocked by both chemotypes, together with a larger voltage-clamp Ih density, would move HCN from "contributes" to "differs"; absent that, no HCN-directed compound is ranked.

corrections_it40: Predictions in the arms are INFERENZA from the hypothesis definitions; no cell is a measured result.
status: survives as a design control, strengthened: the probable absence of synaptic blockers in the intrinsic recordings is an inference from the Methods drug list, not a stated fact; exploratory
starting_observation_and_chain: (1) DATO: neocortical slices burst spontaneously in 36 of 42 KO, 4 of 23 HT and 0 of 11 WT slices (O08); intrinsic properties were recorded in cells that were not spiking spontaneously (O07). -> (2) INFERENZA: the Methods "Pharmacology" paragraph lists only TTX, d-APV, carbenoxolone and brilliant blue FCF and no AMPA or GABA-A antagonist, so the intrinsic recordings were most probably unblocked (not an explicit statement). Synaptic shunting would LOWER Rin (INFERENZA); an effect of raised [K+]o on Rin is IPOTESI (Kir and rectification can act in either direction), so the higher Rin argues against a pure activity-driven state but does not exclude one. -> (3) INFERENZA: HT shows the Rin and rest changes with bursting in a small fraction of slices (the cells are not linked to slices in the paper), but HT slices also differ from WT in mEPSC statistics (pooled-event KS tests, Fig 4 legend), so a synaptic state without bursts is not excluded. -> (4) DATO: pyramidal identity was confirmed using Rin and tau, the outcomes themselves; access resistance up to 40 Mohm was accepted against a Rin of 100-143 Mohm. -> (5) INFERENZA: a selection-independent, maturation-matched comparison under synaptic blockade is the precondition for reading MH1 and MH2; persistence under blockade would show that the difference is intrinsic to the recorded neuron membrane, not that Wwox acts cell-autonomously (the Cre is pan-neuronal; that needs sparse or mosaic deletion). The cell-context axis (layer, maturation stage) remains open. -> (6) benefit: none; it protects the interpretation of pharmacological arms.
context: Same mouse model and slices; additional contexts: layer V pyramidal neurons, an age series around P13-P17, and recordings in WT versus KO slices under synaptic blockade and with unblocked synaptic transmission.
competing_explanations: MH1 or MH2 as genuine cell-autonomous differences; A04 maturation delay (predicts smaller sag); A07 cell-type mix.
premise_and_action: None. It is a design-control hypothesis: repeat the intrinsic-property measurements under synaptic blockade, with identity by morphology or marker, Ra and bridge balance reported by genotype, and an age series (for example P10 to P17) plus layer V.
catalogue_by_action: no relation searched (no pharmacological action proposed)
source_and_limits: HT changes with little bursting; F-I slope unchanged; but no datum on blockade (beyond the probable absence of blockers), identity by morphology or access resistance by genotype exists in the paper. || weakening: Under synaptic blockade, with identity by morphology or marker and matched access resistance, the genotype contrast in Rin, rest and sag is unchanged -> the difference is intrinsic to the recorded membrane and independent of selection; if it shrinks or vanishes, the original contrast was partly synaptic state or selection. Wwox cell-autonomy is not tested by this experiment.
decision_measure: An explicit statement from the authors that intrinsic properties were recorded with or without synaptic blockers (the Methods list is only indirect evidence); recordings under blockade with matched access resistance; sparse or mosaic deletion for cell-autonomy.
